story.title: The Sky Is Torn
story.text: Holes opened in the sky, and wind and rain poured through.
story.narration: Long, long ago, great holes opened in the sky. Wind and rain poured down through them, and the people were cold and afraid.

story.title: Stones of Five Colours
story.text: Nuwa smelted stones of five colours to mend the sky.
story.narration: Nuwa smelted stones of five colours. She would fit them, one by one, into the holes in the sky.

keyMoment.question: How should the holes in the sky be mended?

options.text: Wait for them to heal by themselves
Smelt five-coloured stones and fit them in, one by one

keyMoment.reveal: She smelted the stones of five colours and mended the sky, piece by piece.

misconceptions: The holes would close on their own
One big stone would be enough

quiz.question: What did Nuwa use to mend the sky?
quiz.explanation: She smelted stones of five colours and used them to fill the holes.

quiz.question: How did Nuwa mend the sky?
options: She asked someone else to do it
quiz.explanation: She filled the holes one by one, and the sky grew brighter with each.

quiz.question: Which of these is most like Nuwa mending the sky?
options: Sewing up a hole in your clothes, stitch by stitch
quiz.explanation: Both repair what is torn, a little at a time.

orbs.speak: The blue stone filled the round hole
The red stone filled the square hole
The yellow stone filled the pointed hole
The white stone filled the diamond hole
The purple stone filled the star-shaped hole
